$schema-note: Expansion modules. data/cards.json is the BASE GAME and is frozen: 111 cards,
13 sheets, and decks that have been sent to a printing service. Nothing in
this file may change a card face in that one, and nothing here counts toward
its 111. That is why this is a separate file rather than more keys over there.
What is NOT here on purpose: the Marks themselves. Their rules live in
js/game/marks.js, which the engine reads, and copying them into JSON would
give one fact two homes and let them drift. The reference cards are printed
FROM that table. Everything in this file is content the engine has no opinion
about: which hazards exist, and what each biome hands you.

modules.name: Terrain
modules.rule: A hazard is a place. At the start of each round, any figure standing in it takes its Mark. Once per level you may spend one action to shove the boss or a minion into it.
modules.$note: One rule covers all eight, which is the only reason eight is affordable. Where a figure is standing is fiction the table agrees on: movement is free in this game and there is no board, so a hazard needs no geometry, only a brick on the table and a Mark when someone is in it.

hazard.flavour: Black, slow and patient. Whatever steps in stays a while.

hazard.name: Thorn Nest
hazard.flavour: Every branch of it wants something.

modules.name: Wits
modules.rule: Three cards that live in your hand beside Strike and Focus, for the turns you would rather find something out than hit something.
modules.$note: They are CARDS, not buttons, and that is load-bearing. This is the module for the child who does not reach for the attack cards, so its options have to be lying in front of them next to the ones that do. It also buys the whole interface for free: all three resolve through attack(), so the hand, the plan lane, the target chips, the inspector, the roll dialog, the Rune and the Hunter's reroll already work on them with no new view code. They carry `module`, which legalAttacks and attack() both refuse under legacy, and they live here rather than in cards.json so they never enter the frozen 111.

attack.name: Scout
attack.text: Throw the boss's die now, face up. That is the reaction it will make this round.

attack.name: Analyze
attack.text: Study the boss or one minion: it is Marked, and attacks against it are one step easier.

attack.name: Parley
attack.text: Talk to it. It loses its action this round. Fail and it Roars at you instead.

aid.name: Scout Board
aid.text: Six rows, one per face. Scout throws the boss's die, you stand a brick on the row it landed on, and the die comes back to you for your own checks.

modules.name: Preparation
modules.tagline: Wind up, and hope it lands.
modules.rule: Prepare is the last action of your turn: you are Charged, and your next landed attack deals +50. A prop is one big thing in the room you can knock over, once, and it shares the level's single object slot with the biome's own.
modules.$note: Charged was dead code before this module: marks.js defined it, attackBonus already added it, applyHit already spent it and take() already stripped it, and nothing in the game could place it. M2 is the door, which is why it is one action rather than a subsystem. The LAST-ACTION clause is the whole bet: a Charge cashable on the turn you take it makes Prepare a strictly better Strike, and one design measured turtle level 1 going 67.7 to 100.0 with it unrestricted. The props deliberately share Terrain's objectUsed slot, so a level still has exactly one object and exactly one use, and useObject() needs no change at all.

attack.name: Prepare
attack.text: The last action of your turn. You are Charged: your next landed attack deals +50, and you lose it the moment a hit costs you a card.

modules.name: The Boss Seat
modules.tagline: Somebody has been rolling that die.
modules.rule: The boss's die becomes six cards, one per face. The boss player holds a hand, commits one face down before the hero acts, and turns it over when the boss acts. The hand size is the handicap.
modules.$note: The engine is untouched: reveal() hands bossRoll the same 1..6 a die would, so every reaction, signature, Rage and Brace branch is byte-identical and legacy never sees a seat. Three things differ from the first design, each because a review measured it: the sweep fires when the HAND empties rather than the pile (with a hand of 3 the pile ran dry two rounds early), the Row is swept every THREE cards rather than six (fights are 3.4 to 5.5 rounds, so a six-card cycle never completed and drawing without replacement measured EASIER than the die), and the module makes no claim that the seat cannot hit harder than a die. A second player choosing well should be harder. The handicap is the hand size.

reaction.name: Brace
reaction.text: It digs in. No damage, and it halves what it takes until the end of your next turn.

reaction.name: Strike
reaction.text: It hits you for its Damage.

reaction.name: Strike
reaction.text: It hits you for its Damage. The die has two of these, so the deck does too.

reaction.name: Summon
reaction.text: It splits: two of its life cards move under a new figure.

reaction.name: Roar
reaction.text: It hits you for its Damage, and your next check is one step harder.

reaction.name: Ruin
reaction.text: Double Damage. It may not be the first card of a fight.

aid.name: The Seat
aid.text: How the seat works, for the person holding the cards: commit face down before the hero acts, turn it over when the boss acts, sweep the Row after three.
